chunks: Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) that he said:
Verily when a believer dies, he sees the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and ʿAlī (peace be upon him) present before him.

key_terms.بِحَضْرَتِهِ: present before him / in his presence

ai.seo_question: What does a believer see when they die according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd* emphasizes the intimate spiritual bond between the believer and the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically highlighting the presence of Imam ʿAlī alongside the Prophet at the hour of death. In Shia tradition, this vision serves as a sign of divine favor and the believer's readiness for the transition to the barzakh, reflecting the concept of *wilayah* extending beyond earthly life. The presence of these two figures underscores their unique status as intercessors and guides in the intermediate realm.
